title: Solutions Architect
description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model - which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Role

Every Celonis outcome starts with data. As a Solutions Architect, you make sure our customers’ data gets into the Celonis Platform reliably, securely, and at scale, and that insights and actions flow back out into the systems and AI tools where work actually happens.

You’ll join our customer programs team as one of the first technical faces of Celonis. You’ll work hands-on across the full integration toolkit: deploying our out-of-the-box extractors, building custom API connectors in a low-code environment, writing code for push-based ingestion, connecting Celonis to customer lakehouses and LLMs, and configuring writebacks, SSO, and user provisioning. Part implementation consultant, part integration engineer, part trusted technical advisor, this role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants broad exposure to enterprise architecture and modern data and AI integration patterns.

What You’ll Do

Data integration and ingestion

• Implement standard extractors. Install, configure, and troubleshoot Celonis out-of-the-box extractors in customer landscapes, including SAP (ECC and S/4HANA), JDBC-based databases, and cloud applications such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and others.

• Build custom API connectors. Design and build custom connectors with Celonis Extractor Builder for source systems that expose data through REST or SOAP APIs, handling authentication (OAuth 2.0, API keys, certificates), pagination, rate limits, and incremental (delta) loads.

• Enable push-based ingestion. Help customers design and develop scripts and pipelines (typically in Python) that push data to Celonis via the Data Ingestion API, and advise on file formats, scheduling, and error handling.

• Connect to the lakehouse. Set up zero-copy data sharing between Celonis and customer lakehouses such as Databricks and Microsoft Fabric, including Delta Sharing configuration, access controls, and data freshness.

Actions, AI, and platform connectivity

• Close the loop with writebacks. Configure Action Flows and other integration patterns that write back to customer systems (for example, updating records in SAP, Salesforce, or ticketing tools) so Celonis insights turn into action.

• Connect Celonis to AI. Help customers connect Celonis to their LLMs and AI agents through MCP, covering authentication, permissions, and governance.

Identity, security, and governance

• Own authentication and provisioning. Configure SSO (SAML, OIDC) with identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Ping, and set up SCIM-based user and group provisioning.

• Be the security translator. Support customer security, privacy, and compliance reviews, explain the Celonis architecture and data flows, and advise on topics like data minimization, pseudonymization, and least-privilege access.

Customer and team impact

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast. The role You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap. Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Plaid's Connectivity team builds and operates the network that powers open finance, connecting consumers' financial accounts to the apps and services they choose to use across thousands of institutions. Where an institution offers an API, we use it. Where one doesn't, we still need a dependable, secure way to honor a consumer's request to share their own data. The Alternative Access team owns that path: the client, network and reliability systems that make consumer-permissioned connections work when no API is available.

You will be the hands-on technical lead for alternative access. You will set its direction and build the systems yourself: browser- and mobile-based clients that act on the consumer's behalf, the network egress infrastructure those sessions run through, credential and session handling, and the measurement that tells us how well it all works.

Institutions' traffic controls often cannot distinguish a consumer-directed session from unwanted automation. You will study how real clients behave at the browser, device and network level, and make permissioned sessions faithful to that behavior so that consumers' connections stay reliable as institutions change.

You will turn today's approach into a platform that can be extended to new institutions in weeks, decide where to build versus buy, and partner closely with Legal, Policy, Security and Product so that every method we deploy is one we're confident in. This is a role with direct visibility to Plaid's leadership and a clear path to leading the area.

Responsibilities:

- You'll design, build and operate the production systems that let consumers share data from institutions without an API.

- You'll research how browsers, mobile apps and networks present themselves to institutions and keep permissioned sessions consistent with real client behavior.

- You'll build and run egress and proxy infrastructure, and evaluate routing approaches and vendors on effectiveness, cost and risk.

- You'll instrument success rate, breakage detection and time to repair, and drive staged rollouts with Product and Account Management.

- You'll write the design and risk documentation that lets leadership make deployment decisions, and bring Legal, Policy and Security in early.

- You'll mentor engineers and raise the technical bar across Connectivity through design reviews and hands-on work.

Qualifications:

- 6+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on work building and operating systems that act on a user's behalf against third-party web or mobile applications at scale.

- Deep knowledge of browser internals and automation (Chromium, Chrome DevTools Protocol, Playwright or Puppeteer) or of mobile application internals and instrumentation.

- Experience-based understanding of traffic classification and fingerprinting (device, browser, TLS and network signals, behavioral signals).

- Experience designing and operating network egress and proxy infrastructure.

- Strong reliability instincts: you instrument what you build and find breakage before users do.

- Security-minded handling of credentials and sessions, and sound judgment about what to build, not just what is possible.

We are looking for an experienced MCAT Tutor to provide one-on-one MCAT preparation to students. You will teach all sections of the MCAT, develop individualized study plans, and track student progress throughout their preparation.

• Tutor students one-on-one across all sections of the MCAT

• Develop and adapt MCAT study plans based on each student's needs and performance

• Track and analyze student progress and performance

• Create and maintain project trackers to monitor MCAT preparation progress

• Keep students' families up to date on academic progress and MCAT milestones

• Provide guidance on MCAT content, strategy, and test-taking skills

• 2+ years of MCAT tutoring or MCAT test-preparation experience
